gddGap: The GDD says "urban districts" and "Defeat Wave / Clear Arena ... in time" but sets no level count, order, wave counts or time limit. Level 1 is paced as a tutorial arc (warm-up, pressure, first Breaker, escalation, finale) with health pickups in the breathers; wave numbers and the 210 s limit are design assumptions, not GDD-confirmed.
name: Brick-Red Alley
theme: Zed's home alley: brick walls, a mustard corner shop, mural panels and an open window with music.
intro: Home. The alley where Zed learned to fight, dance and argue like family. Push the Rust back and let the block breathe.
outro: The alley is ours again. A window cracks open and a record starts to play. Zed grins. Next stop, Mustard Row.

gddGap: No level structure in the GDD. Fields the Rust Watcher (rust-watcher) in repeated waves and the Rust Breaker (rust-breaker) as the closer, with grunts, so the player must use lane movement so the player must use lane movement. Also fields the named Overseer Dr. Maren Holt (rust-overseer-holt) as the district boss wave; the GDD gives Holt an undercity lab arena with gas vents and fog, so the garden planters and food-stall fog are only the closest fit (no GDD level for her; flag). Engine waves hold one enemy type each and counts cannot shrink, so the Holt wave keeps count 5 with maxAlive 1 (an engine workaround: Holt is a single named character, and a count of 1 would break the non-decreasing wave-count rule) until boss-encounter waves exist (further gap). 180 s limit assumed.
